xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4223: Official gauntlet loop support: pan lane (launch/list/wait/report/reap), lanes nested under their orchestrator, any-harness orchestrators

plan.title: Official gauntlet loop support: pan lane (launch/list/wait/report/reap), lanes nested under their orchestrator, any-harness orchestrators
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: The operator filed and decided this as one feature (PRD Q1-Q3: verb, reap-archives, successor nesting) and then extended it in one comment (the builder-critic link, FR-31 to FR-38), and the parts interlock: the lane door, the parent-link and critic-link schema, the fork stamp, the verdict reports and the two nesting views share one data contract (parent_conversation_id, critic_of_conversation_id and three lane columns). The documentation work alone spans more than 6 lint subsystems (reference/, configuration/, docs/, sync-sources/, CLAUDE.md, docs.json), so no split into sibling issues passes the projected-surface gate cleanly, and the first item is already in progress on this branch. The plan compensates with 38 small items, an explicit DAG, and four inspected foundation items.

narratives.Problem: Gauntlet orchestrators fan out lanes by hand. Claude orchestrators use the Agent tool (Anthropic models only); other models abuse `pan handoff` from a throwaway conversation because handoff ignores --harness. The result is about a dozen flat 'SB lane: …' conversations parented (inside fork_request JSON) to the wrong row, a hand-rolled sentinel.log completion signal, duplicate lanes sharing a worktree, runaway lanes nobody sees, and manual teardown. GPT, Codex and Kimi orchestrators cannot fan out at all.
narratives.Proposal: Follow .pan/drafts/pan-4223.md. A lane is an ordinary conversation carrying four write-once launch-time columns (parent_conversation_id, gauntlet_run, lane_key, lane_role); lane status is derived on read. One core (launchLane) behind POST /api/lanes and `pan lane start` creates the per-lane worktree under a configurable lanes root, writes the brief, and starts a conversation with any harness/model/effort through the extracted startConversationRuntime. `pan lane list|wait|report|stop|reap` reuse the worker report and wait machinery, the conversation stop door and the archive door (reap archives by default, --keep retains). handleConversationSummaryFork stamps the parent link so handoff/fork successors nest. The Command Deck and the Agents page nest rows by parent link, capped at display depth 2. pan tell resolves a conversation's real harness and refuses to re-task a critic that reported. The pan-gauntlet-loop skill adopts the lane door and the GAUNTLET-LOOP-V3 rules. A critic lane links the builder row it judges (critic_of_conversation_id, required via --for for critics), files one verdict through `pan lane report --verdict`, and the pairing (critics per builder iteration, the answered verdict, the `pan lane show` chain) is derived by one pure module and shown by the lanes API, `pan lane list`/`show`, the Command Deck (critic nested under its builder with verdict badges) and the Agents page, while the critic is told nothing about the builder.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Serving the gauntlet progress page from the dashboard; the skill's http.server page stays.
- Modeling board statuses (ACCEPTED, SHIPPED, …), merges or releases in Overdeck; they stay in the project repo. Verdicts are read from critic reports and paired, but never turned into a board status.
- Injecting anything from a builder (transcript, reasoning, brief, report text, conversation name) into its critic.
- Parsing critique-<area>-iter<n>.json for the verdict value; the file is linked by path (read only for an optional defect count).
- A stored verdict or pairing column beyond the single write-once critic_of_conversation_id link.
- Machine-level rig limits (browser slots, ports, displays); they stay in the project's run file.
- Changing pan handoff, pan fork or pan worker behavior beyond the parent link on fork successors and cross-reference docs; a handoff of a lane does not carry lane facts to its successor.
- A per-run Herdr workspace or a parent pane token.
- Automatic lane launching or scheduling; the orchestrator decides every launch.
- Re-parenting or backfilling existing rows (including HOTEL conversations 2899-2910).
- Parent links on post-/clear siblings, backfilled agent rows, retrospective conversations or POST /api/conversations rows.
- A stored lane status field or a run table.
- Accepting effort xhigh at the lane door.
- Killing any process during reap, or `git worktree remove --force`.
- A `pan lane tell` verb (messaging stays `pan tell`).

autoDecisions.summary: Keep PAN-4223 as one issue and set plan.metadata.sizeJustification instead of filing sibling issues.
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator filed and decided the design as one unit; the docs item alone exceeds the 6-subsystem lint limit, so a split cannot pass the gate cleanly; 24 small items with explicit edges keep review granular.

autoDecisions.summary: Split PRD work items WI-3, WI-5, WI-6, WI-10, WI-11 and WI-13 into smaller xBRIEF items; move the reap route from WI-5 into the reap item.
autoDecisions.rationale: The planning rules require the smallest defensible items; the reap route imports reapLane, so it belongs with WI-7.

autoDecisions.summary: Run frontend tests through `npm --prefix ./src/dashboard/frontend run test -- <paths>` and corrected AC-10/AC-11 in the PRD.
autoDecisions.rationale: The root vitest.config.ts excludes src/dashboard/frontend/**, so the PRD's root `npx vitest run` commands for frontend files would run nothing.

autoDecisions.summary: Only lane-columns (conversations.ts, at its 1111 cap) and runtime-start-extract (conversation-runtime.ts, at its 1186 cap) own scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt, ordered by an edge; cli/index.ts (cap 1379) and projects.ts (cap 1210) have headroom and the reap change adds no lines to routes/conversations.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: scripts/lint-file-size.sh fails a file only above its allowlisted cap; limiting the shared allowlist to the two capped files avoids needless serialization.

autoDecisions.summary: The lane door passes `undefined` as the explicit harness when neither --harness nor gauntlet.roles config names one.
autoDecisions.rationale: concerns.md records that coalescing to 'claude-code' bypasses the provider default in resolveHarness; the PRD's any-harness goal depends on the provider default applying.

autoDecisions.summary: The AC-10 live Command Deck screenshot is a test/UAT-role check, not a work-item gate; work items do not run `pan reload`.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD already names the component tests as the gate with the screenshot as a fallback-at-next-reload; only the flywheel deploys.

autoDecisions.summary: Re-plan for the operator's builder-critic comment by adding new items and leaving the in-progress lane-columns item (WI-1) unchanged; revise only pending items whose text the comment overturns (lane-contract, tell-fixes, gauntlet-skill, docs-reference).
autoDecisions.rationale: lane-columns is claimed with uncommitted work; changing its scope would strand the claim, while new items keep every change reviewable on its own.

autoDecisions.summary: Reverse the D10 sentence and non-goal 'Overdeck does not model verdicts': verdicts are read from the critic's done report and paired with builder iterations; board statuses stay out.
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator's comment, which postdates the PRD, requires list/API/show to return WOWED / NOT_YET / pending; it is an amendment, not a contradiction between authoritative inputs.

autoDecisions.summary: Store one write-once column, critic_of_conversation_id (the judged builder row's UUID), not critic_of_lane_key.
autoDecisions.rationale: The comment allows either; the UUID pins the exact row and the key, run and iteration derive through a join (D26).

autoDecisions.summary: The verdict travels in the critic's report via `pan lane report --verdict <WOWED|IMPRESSED|NOT_YET|PASS|DEFECTS> [--defects n] [--verdict-file path]`; a second done report from a critic is refused.
autoDecisions.rationale: The report store survives reap and is keyed by the critic's conversation; the critique file's path and shape are project conventions (D24). The vocabulary is V3's.

autoDecisions.summary: Pair critics with builder iterations (not rows); the answered verdict of builder i(n) is the newest critic of i(n-1) created before it; UI nesting uses the exact linked row.
autoDecisions.rationale: D7 makes a --reuse respawn a second row of the same iteration; pairing by iteration keeps its critics (D25).

autoDecisions.summary: --for is required for critics and optional for verifiers; it defaults --key to the builder key and --at to the builder iteration's newest done-report head.
autoDecisions.rationale: The comment scopes the requirement to critics; V3 verifiers may judge a whole run (D29); the head default ties the critic to the judged iteration (FR-32).

autoDecisions.summary: Add a seventh subcommand `pan lane show [lane] | --run --key` for the chain; `pan lane show 663` is not accepted because a bare number is a conversation id.
autoDecisions.rationale: The comment names `pan lane show <builder>`; accepting --run/--key avoids an id/key ambiguity.

autoDecisions.summary: The Agents Live view keeps one child level: a critic line follows its builder line inside the same row's children, one indent deeper.
autoDecisions.rationale: LiveRow.children is a flat DirectoryEntry[] and builders are already child lines (WI-11); this meets 'critic appears as a child of its builder' without reshaping the row model (D27).

autoDecisions.summary: Verdict badges: WOWED and PASS use the done token; NOT_YET, DEFECTS, IMPRESSED and PENDING use the neutral badge.
autoDecisions.rationale: pan-style-guide bans decorative color; a verdict asking for another iteration is routine work, not an alarm (D28).

narrative.Action: Implement .pan/drafts/pan-4223.md WI-1 exactly. Add parent_conversation_id, gauntlet_run, lane_key and lane_role to the conversations table in drizzle/overdeck/0000_overdeck_init.sql (plus conversations_parent_idx and conversations_gauntlet_run_idx) and as idempotent runSchemaTopUp calls at the end of ensureRuntimeIndexesSync in src/lib/overdeck/infra.ts. In src/lib/overdeck/conversations.ts export LaneRole and LANE_ROLES; extend LegacyConversationRow, LEGACY_CONVERSATION_SELECT (LEFT JOIN conversations p ON p.id = c.parent_conversation_id; qualify every following WHERE/ORDER BY column with c.), LegacyConversation and rowToLegacyConversation with parentConversationId (legacy rowid), parentConversationName, gauntletRun, laneKey, laneRole. createConversation accepts parentName and lane and writes them in the same INSERT (unknown parent throws 'parent conversation <name> not found'; lane without parentName throws 'a lane needs a parent'). Add listLaneConversations(filter) (archived rows included, lane_key set only, created_at order) and resolveEffectiveLauncher(name) per D21 with a visited-set guard. Mirror the columns in docs/overdeck-remodel/overdeck-schema.ts. Write src/lib/overdeck/__tests__/conversation-lane-columns.test.ts with every case the PRD lists. If conversations.ts grows past its file-size cap, append a '<lines> src/lib/overdeck/conversations.ts # PAN-4223' row to scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt.

items.title: Given createConversation is called with parentName and lane { run, key, role }, when the row is read back with getConversationByName, then it returns parentConversationName, parentConversationId (the parent's legacy rowid), gauntletRun, laneKey and laneRole with the stored values.

Given createConversation is called with parentName and no lane, then the row stores the parent link and returns gauntletRun, laneKey and laneRole as null; an unknown parentName throws 'parent conversation <name> not found' and inserts no row.
resolveEffectiveLauncher returns the orchestrator lane for a successor→successor→orchestrator-lane chain, returns the root for a successor→successor→root chain, and returns a root unchanged.
listLaneConversations({ run }) returns that run's lanes oldest first, includes an archived lane, and excludes a successor of one of the run's lanes.

ensureRuntimeIndexesSync adds the four columns to a database created without them, and a second run exits silently; `grep -c parent_conversation_id` reports at least 1 in both 0000_overdeck_init.sql and infra.ts.

Add the async git worktree helpers for lanes (WI-3 part)

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/lanes/worktree.ts per .pan/drafts/pan-4223.md WI-3 step 3, using promisified execFile with a 60 s timeout on every git call (never execSync; the module is dashboard-server reachable). Export fetchBase(projectPath) (git fetch origin; a failure returns a warning string and does not throw), addBranchWorktree(projectPath, path, branch, base) (existing local branch → `git worktree add <path> <branch>`, else `git worktree add -b <branch> <path> <base>`), addDetachedWorktree(projectPath, path, ref) (`git worktree add --detach`), applySparse(path, patterns) (`git -C <path> sparse-checkout set --no-cone …`) and a laneDirName validator for `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$`. Module header cites .pan/drafts/pan-4223.md. Test against a real temporary git repo in src/lib/lanes/__tests__/worktree.test.ts.

items.title: Given a temp repo, addBranchWorktree creates a worktree on a new branch cut from the base, and a second call for an existing branch creates the worktree on that branch without -b.
addDetachedWorktree creates a worktree whose HEAD is detached at the requested commit.
Given a fetch failure, fetchBase returns a warning string and does not throw; laneDirName rejects 'Bad/Name' and accepts 'hotel-663-i2'.
Add the lane contract text builder (WI-3 part)

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/lanes/contract.ts exporting laneContract({ role, run, key, iteration, briefPath, cwd, branch, at, answering }) that returns exactly the text in .pan/drafts/pan-4223.md WI-3 step 5 (as revised 2026-09-26): the common header and rules (including 'pan lane report --file <that file>' and the RULING/SPEND/ONE-WAY/BLOCKED first-line rule) followed by the one role block for builder, critic/verifier, play or orchestrator, with placeholders filled. The critic/verifier block tells the lane to report once with `pan lane report --file <report> --verdict <value> --verdict-file <verdict JSON> [--defects <n>]` and never names the builder's conversation (FR-38). For a builder, a non-null `answering` ({ criticId, role, iteration, verdict, file }) adds the line 'This iteration answers <role> c<iteration> (conv #<criticId>): <verdict>. Verdict file: <file or "none recorded">.' ('v' instead of 'c' for a verifier). Module header cites .pan/drafts/pan-4223.md. Write src/lib/lanes/__tests__/contract.test.ts.

items.title: For each of the five roles, laneContract returns text that contains 'pan lane report --file' and that role's block (critic and verifier share one block).
The builder text contains the branch name passed in, and the critic text contains the `at` commit passed in plus '--verdict' and '--verdict-file'.

Given a builder with answering { criticId: 42, role: 'critic', iteration: 1, verdict: 'NOT_YET', file: '/x/v.json' }, laneContract returns text containing 'answers critic c1 (conv #42): NOT_YET'; given answering null it returns no 'answers' line.

items.title: Given a builder launch for run hotel key 663 from a root parent, launchLane creates <root>/hotel-663 on branch hotel/663 from origin/main, writes lane-brief.md once, stores the four lane columns, titles the row 'hotel 663 · builder', and calls startConversationRuntime with the builder contract.

launchLane rejects with 400 a critic without --at, a critic launched from a lane parent, a successor of an orchestrator lane launching a critic, effort 'xhigh', a lanes root under /tmp or equal to the project path, and a launch with no model anywhere (message names the gauntlet.roles config key).

Given a successor of an orchestrator lane launches a builder, the builder inherits the orchestrator lane's run and its parent link names the successor; a successor of a root orchestrator launches a critic with 201.

Given a live builder for the same (run, key), launchLane returns 409 naming it; with replace it stops the old lane first and counts a new iteration; two concurrent launches for the same (run, key, role) produce exactly one success and one 409.

Given an i1 builder row whose newest report branch is hotel/663, a new builder launch creates <root>/hotel-663-i2 on new branch hotel/663-i2 cut from hotel/663; with reuse no git worktree add runs and the iteration equals the reused row's; a play launch creates a plain directory with bareContext and skipClaudeMd set.

Implement reportLane with the builder clean-and-pushed guard (WI-6 part 3)

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/lanes/report.ts reportLane({ body, status, allowUnpushed }, env) per .pan/drafts/pan-4223.md WI-6 step 3. items.title: Given OVERDECK_CONVERSATION names a non-lane conversation (including a lane's successor), reportLane rejects with 'not inside a lane'.

Implement single-lane and lane-set waits (WI-6 part 4)

expected_outputs: wait.test.ts exits 0 with fake time only
